summary: Describes how the protocols in the signalling transport framework apply, including the main issues with using SCTP and an explanation of each adaptation layer for carrying telephony signalling over IP. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This is a guide for choosing the right adapter to carry phone-network control messages over the internet, and when to use each one.

subtitle: How to carry telephone control signals over the internet using SCTP.

tldr.problem: Telephone signalling protocols are designed for dedicated circuits and have strict timing and reliability requirements that the public internet does not naturally provide.
tldr.mechanism: SIGTRAN (Signalling Transport) defines SCTP, a reliable message-oriented protocol, plus User Adaptation Layers that wrap telephone signalling so it can travel over IP while preserving its required timing and ordering properties.
tldr.outcome: Telephone networks can now interconnect with IP networks and IP-based switching equipment without losing the signal reliability and ordering that telephone signalling requires.

facts.label: Key feature
facts.value: Multiple independent streams to avoid head-of-line blocking

today: RFC 4166 is an Informational RFC providing applicability guidance for SIGTRAN protocols. SIGTRAN remains the standard framework for carrying telephone signalling over IP, and is widely deployed by telecommunications carriers for NGN (Next Generation Network) implementations.

sections.title: Bridging Phone and IP Networks
sections.content:
SIGTRAN (Signalling Transport) is a framework for carrying telephone signalling protocols over IP networks. Traditional telephone signalling, used to set up and tear down calls, relies on dedicated signalling circuits with guaranteed delivery order and timing. The internet does not offer these guarantees by default. SIGTRAN solves this by combining SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol), a new transport protocol designed for telephony, with a set of User Adaptation Layers (UALs) that wrap existing telephone signalling protocols so they work correctly over SCTP.

The architecture has four layers: at the top are the telephone signalling protocols themselves (such as ISUP for calls or SS7 for routing); then come the User Adaptation Layers that translate these protocols; then SCTP, the transport; and finally IP at the bottom. Each adaptation layer preserves the same interface that the original telephone signalling layer provided, so equipment does not have to change how it speaks to the layer above.
sections.eli5: Phone networks have their own language for setting up calls. The internet has a different language. SIGTRAN is a translator that sits between them, turning phone language into internet packets and back, so they can talk to each other.

sections.title: How SCTP Supports Telephony
sections.content:
SCTP was designed from the ground up for telephony signalling. Unlike TCP, which delivers bytes in a stream, SCTP preserves message boundaries, so each signalling message arrives as a complete unit. SCTP offers multiple streams within a single connection, so different message sequences can be sent independently without one lost message blocking others—a problem called head-of-line blocking in TCP.

SCTP provides reliable data transfer, so messages arrive exactly once and in order within each stream. It includes congestion control and flow control to avoid overwhelming the network, but telephony applications must be aware that this can introduce delays during congestion. SCTP supports multi-homing, allowing endpoints to maintain multiple network paths for redundancy, and it includes continuous monitoring of peer reachability via heartbeat mechanisms.

The protocol also includes protections against denial-of-service attacks and blind masquerade attacks. Critically for telephony, SCTP allows the application to customize key parameters such as the minimum retransmission timeout (RTO.Min) and heartbeat interval to meet strict timing requirements, though lowering these values may stress the network during congestion.
sections.eli5: SCTP is like a post office designed for phone calls. It makes sure messages arrive complete and in order. It can use many mail routes at the same time without one slow route holding up all the others. It also checks that the person sending is real, and watches to make sure the connection is still alive.

sections.title: User Adaptation Layers for Different Signalling
sections.content:
User Adaptation Layers translate between specific telephone signalling protocols and SCTP. Access signalling protocols control connections between a subscriber's equipment and the central office. The most common is Q.931 (ISDN), wrapped by the IUA (ISDN User Adaptation) layer. V5UA carries V5.2 signalling for analog and ISDN access, and DUA adapts DPNSS/DASS2 signalling.

Network signalling or trunk signalling is used between telephone switches in the core network. The SS7 protocol stack is the standard here. M2UA carries SS7's MTP3 level over SCTP by terminating MTP2 at a Signalling Gateway and MTP3 at an application server. M2PA (MTP2-User Peer-to-Peer) allows IP-based equipment to speak SS7 directly to each other or to traditional SS7 nodes. M3UA carries MTP3-User protocols (like ISUP) directly. SUA (SCCP User Adaptation) carries SCCP-User protocols such as MAP and RANAP.

Two main deployment scenarios use these layers: SG-to-AS (Signalling Gateway to Application Server) interworking, where a traditional telephone switch connects to IP-based equipment, and IPSP-to-IPSP (IP Signalling Point to IP Signalling Point), where two IP-based switches communicate directly over IP networks.
sections.eli5: There are many different telephone signalling languages. Each adapter speaks one specific language on the top and turns it into SCTP packets on the bottom. Q.931 is for customer phone lines, SS7 is for the phone backbone, and there are adapters for each.

sections.title: Performance and Configuration Issues
sections.content:
Telephony applications often need short end-to-end message delays and rapid failure detection. The RFC identifies several areas where SCTP's defaults may conflict with these requirements. Congestion control may delay messages unacceptably during network stress; in a well-engineered private network, applications may relax SCTP's congestion control if they implement their own. Retransmission timeout (RTO) parameters directly affect how quickly the sender detects that a message failed; lowering RTO.Min speeds detection but risks false positives during network congestion on the public internet.

Heartbeat intervals control how quickly the protocol detects when a path becomes unreachable. Maximum retransmission counts affect both failure detection speed and the risk of false alarms. Bundling (combining small messages into one packet) saves bandwidth but adds delay to some messages. Stream usage should split independent signalling sequences into separate streams to avoid head-of-line blocking.

There is no universal right answer: the correct settings depend on the telephony application, the network characteristics, and the risk tolerance for false failure detection. Implementers must balance the needs of timing requirements, network stability, and reliability.
sections.eli5: SCTP can be tuned with dials and knobs. Turn one dial to find lost messages faster, but it might get confused in traffic jams. Turn another to separate different conversations so one slow one does not freeze the others. Every operator has to pick the settings that fit their telephone network.

sections.title: Security and Deployment
sections.content:
SIGTRAN protocols carry the signalling that controls telephone calls, so security is critical. The protocols themselves do not implement encryption or authentication; instead, security depends on SCTP parameters, underlying network security (IPsec or TLS), and administrative controls. Implementers should follow the security considerations defined in each specific User Adaptation Layer protocol.

SCTP itself includes mechanisms to reduce the risk of blind denial-of-service attacks. However, end-to-end security requires additional layers. IPsec is the primary security mechanism recommended for SIGTRAN on the public internet; TLS over SCTP is an alternative for specific scenarios. Both approaches require careful configuration and management.
sections.eli5: Because SIGTRAN controls phone calls, it has to be secure. SCTP watches out for fake calls trying to mess things up, but to be truly safe, the telephone network should wrap the whole connection in encryption, just like a bank wraps a package in armour.
